title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed in a city during a major public event without sufficient battery capacity to handle the traffic conditions that resulted. At least a dozen vehicles became immobilized on streets during Fourth of July celebrations when traffic congestion prevented them from reaching charging locations, draining their batteries entirely. Some vehicles required towing to be removed from traffic.

The failure occurred at the boundary between system design and real-world deployment. The vehicles were built to operate within normal traffic patterns but were not tested or equipped for the extreme congestion created by large-scale public events and unplanned road closures. Better traffic modeling, event-specific operational planning, or dynamic battery management before the peak congestion would have prevented the stranding.

It is not established whether Waymo knew this traffic scenario was possible in the area, whether the company had an event contingency plan, or what specific design changes would prevent recurrence.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on city streets when their batteries drained while stuck in severe traffic following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets with some requiring towing assistance. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion in the area.

The incident sparked frustration among other drivers, with one person reporting spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic and witnessing people yelling at the autonomous vehicles due to the lack of human drivers. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. The company stated it is evaluating ways to improve its vehicles' resilience during major traffic disruptions. San Francisco officials indicated they plan to discuss the incident with public and private partners to improve future traffic management during large events.
